neighbours.label: an opening quotation mark that introduces a quote mid-sentence after a speech verb (said that “…)
fire: The coach told reporters that “we simply ran out of energy.”
In a statement, the company said “safety is our top priority.”
The witness insisted that “nobody left the building.”
Her lawyer argued “the evidence was never there.”
The minister added that “talks will continue next week.”
When asked about the fire, the chief said “it spread very fast.”
The governor declared that “the state is open for business.”
Speaking at the rally, she promised “we will fix the roads.”
quiet: The coach told reporters that the team simply ran out of energy.
In a statement, the company said safety is its top priority.
The witness insisted that nobody left the building.
Her lawyer argued the evidence was never there.
The minister spoke briefly. “Talks will continue next week,” he added.
The chief arrived at the scene. “It spread very fast,” she said.
The governor declared the state open for business.
Speaking at the rally, she promised to fix the roads.

notes: The + pole fires on an opening quote/bracket at the START of a new sentence; the - pole on one inside a sentence after a speech verb. Two near misses put the quote at sentence start (the other side of the distinction).
